name: Sneddon syndrome
aliases: idiopathic livedo reticularis with cerebrovascular accidents

reference.source: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology / cerebrovascular and rheumatology literature
clinicalPearls: Defined by the combination of widespread livedo racemosa and recurrent ischaemic cerebrovascular events
Livedo is a persistent, broken, irregular net-like violaceous pattern that often precedes strokes by years
Affects predominantly young to middle-aged women and presents with strokes, transient ischaemic attacks, and progressive cognitive decline
A substantial subset have antiphospholipid antibodies, linking it to the antiphospholipid syndrome spectrum
Hypertension, headache, and vascular dementia are frequent accompaniments
Skin biopsy from the border of livedo may show a non-inflammatory occlusive vasculopathy of small dermal arteries
Management centres on antithrombotic therapy and control of vascular risk factors rather than a specific cure
reference.pathophysiology: Sneddon syndrome is a non-inflammatory occlusive arteriopathy affecting small and medium arteries of the skin and brain. Progressive endothelial injury and subintimal proliferation lead to partial then complete occlusion of dermal and cerebral vessels, producing the characteristic livedo racemosa and recurrent cerebral ischaemia. In antiphospholipid-antibody-positive cases a prothrombotic autoimmune mechanism contributes, whereas seronegative cases appear to reflect a primary vasculopathy; both converge on chronic small-vessel occlusion and cumulative brain injury.
additionalDifferentials: Antiphospholipid syndrome without the full livedo picture
Systemic lupus erythematosus and other connective tissue disease
Systemic vasculitis such as polyarteritis nodosa
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and other thrombotic microangiopathies
additionalInvestigations: Antiphospholipid antibody panel including lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I
Brain MRI and MR angiography to document infarcts and small-vessel disease
Skin biopsy taken from the white centre of the livedo net to capture occluded arterioles
Connective tissue and vasculitis serology to exclude alternative causes
Echocardiography and thrombophilia screening to assess embolic and prothrombotic sources
redFlags: Recurrent strokes in a young patient with persistent livedo
Catastrophic thrombotic events suggesting antiphospholipid syndrome
New focal neurological deficits despite antithrombotic therapy
reference.prognosis: The condition tends to be progressive, with recurrent strokes and stepwise cognitive decline leading to vascular dementia in many patients; antithrombotic therapy and risk-factor control may slow but rarely halt the course.
pitfalls: Dismissing livedo racemosa as benign livedo reticularis and missing the underlying vasculopathy
Failing to test for antiphospholipid antibodies, which alters anticoagulation decisions
Taking skin biopsy from the wrong site so the occlusive lesion is missed
Attributing young-onset stroke to a single episode rather than a systemic vasculopathy
references: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
management: Antithrombotic therapy as the mainstay, using antiplatelet agents or anticoagulation with a vitamin K antagonist, particularly in antiphospholipid-antibody-positive patients.
Aggressive vascular risk-factor control including treatment of hypertension, statin therapy and smoking cessation.
Manage co-existing antiphospholipid syndrome according to its thrombotic risk where antibodies are confirmed.
Cognitive assessment and support given the tendency to stepwise vascular cognitive decline.
Surveillance with serial brain imaging, blood pressure monitoring and reassessment after recurrent ischaemic events.
Coordinate care across neurology, dermatology and rheumatology.
Reassess and intensify the antithrombotic strategy after recurrent strokes occurring despite treatment.

annotations.label: Cerebral Parenchyma
annotations.description: Gray-white matter differentiation, cortical ribbon, and deep nuclear structures.

annotations.label: Ventricular System
annotations.description: Lateral, third, and fourth ventricle volume; midline shift and symmetry.

annotations.label: Extra-Axial Spaces
annotations.description: Subarachnoid cisterns, sulcal patency, and calvarial bone margins.
